# Editing one Page caption on a mixed CDX drawing

Prepared 2026-11-20. Bondline owns the generator and all five binary witnesses under MIT OR Apache-2.0. Reproduce the files with `python3 -B crates/io/tests/fixtures/cdx-mixed-caption-edit/generate.py --output-dir <directory>`. With no arguments, the generator verifies all five current files against an independent reconstruction. It uses Python struct, the pinned 320-byte Bondline boxed-label source and the repository’s pinned standalone Python record oracle. Each state is constructed from its original ingredients. The oracle compares all source bytes before and after the one eligible property on every directed edit in the table.

CDX property 0x0700 belongs to a Text object. The selectable caption is direct Page Text. Nodes can own separate Text labels, and the same raw object ID can recur in different scopes. Walk the actual object/parent chain for the current source snapshot and resolve the stable live ID used in the full mixed projection. The target has a persistent Bondline tag, raw Text ID 73 and live ID 19. Two earlier Node-owned labels also have raw Text ID 73. An independent unmarked Page peer has raw ID 9 and live ID 1. The target is first among the two direct captions in encounter order, but renders second. The peer has explicit depth 2 and the target has explicit depth 7. The lower chemical drawing retains its original zero-depth, red NH2 and blue Cl. The target begins with a blue 24 pt H over the red atom-label H. Every expected state keeps the first H at the previously certified overlapping position (158.947265625, 131.65625) pt, so the same red-only, blue-only, and blue-over-red outline samples from the mixed display `overlap_after` case apply. Read them from `crates/io/tests/fixtures/cdx-mixed-caption/cases.json`. Evaluate them at 100% and 200% and compare CPU/GPU full scene captures for the supported viewport. The target has two explicit UTF-8 Roboto runs. Run 0 is 24 pt blue and run 1 is 12 pt reserved black. A CDXString stores the count, unsigned 16-bit start and eight style bytes per run, followed by literal text. Preserve each original style byte, including the color and size. The checked ASCII prefix ensures the next start agrees under byte, scalar and UTF-16 counting. The independent fixtures encode the published short property length for real edits. An unchanged no-op keeps the imported raw property encoding. ## Receiving workflow

1. Open `before.cdx`, check the entire model and original byte association. Set ID 19 run 0 to the longer prefix. Match the entire `after_prefix.cdx`. Then set run 1 to the Unicode tail and match `after_both.cdx`. Independently compare the loaded model, the position/depth/identity tag and every byte outside record 37. In the first change only the second start advances inside the run table. Only the requested literal changes on the second edit.
2. Reverse the first change to get `after_tail.cdx`, then reverse the remaining change to get exact `before.cdx`. Verify source modified state returns to baseline. Exercise Undo and Redo to restore exact snapshots and file-receipt dirty state. Save As to a Unicode path, reopen and edit again with the same live IDs. Starting at `extended_before.cdx`, an identical edit creates zero history and keeps the extended prefix. A real edit emits the short-form expectation. Undo restores the exact extended bytes. A later logical inverse may have the same model and a different original length encoding, so require correct byte-aware source provenance.
3. Require exact owned original record selection, unchanged UTF-8 run styles, checked starts, re-import with the same mixed source classification, expected whole-model equality and a complete paper/render proof before publishing one edit. A stale revision, unknown ID, wrong run, Unicode nonfinal prefix, overlong/off-paper edit, unsupported join and detached model must preserve bytes, revisions, history and file association. Preserve the separate guards for standalone caption-only and atom-label sources and all original mixed unsupported-source diagnostics.
4. Use the same registry command via CLI, MCP and native painted-run targeting. Actual click on a blue-over-red cell must address Page caption 19; an atom-label-only cell or blank paper grants no authoring. Keep mixed creation, selection/nudging, Alt atom edit and cross-format output closed pending their own work. No new registry record or tool is needed. Reuse the existing mixed scope for looking up caption records and keep existing full-profile checks on every writer.
